The two variables are strongly correlated (Pearson r = -0.65), so a relationship exists and D is out. The correlation can't show direction, so I chose A on physical reasoning. Low sea level pressure, meaning cyclonic and storm systems, drives moist-air convergence and lifting, and that produces precipitation. The reverse effect, latent heating from rain lowering the pressure, is much weaker, and I judged the link not to be double-sided.

ANSWER: A
